Azathoth is nothing that is, not-somehow/somehow
Abraxas is Volition without Will
the Empress is Agape coffaw Eros and Agon
Baphomet is S/He 
that Produces Shine who is Shining in the 
Flood


                            The Moon is the Expression of Hagaea


_____________________________________________________________________________________


Thought is gauge and direction, a tragic djinn of breakthroughs.
The confusing matrices, the web of thoughts, affects, somatic and mysterious, scientific and poetic, spiritual and beyond gibberish,
a dank, bright, funky net for fish of newness or at least relief in a storm or depressed drought.

Thought and Volition are phallic positing.
Reception and Solidity are feminine acceptance.
That sounds crude, good; Baphomet is crude, clean, male and female and all the other bio-ontological innovations.



___________________________________________________________________________


The storm isn't wrong, still the Way.
..................................



Say that thought is the problem, cold and clinical, 
and what will it do?

Someone tries to stop thinking, then tries not to try.
Thoughts always fit through the holes in the net.

The matrices, the holes, the thoughts.

Try or don't try.

Thoughts come of themselves.
They are selves?
Thought or no-thought or no thoughts. Self or no selves.

Thoughts and selves are simply what they are.

Only the aeon of psyche, that tragic red herring of my boat
inflicts You like a white void.  . . .
None of this has to be.

I don't even assume thoughts and no-thought as a Thing.

                       The Thing

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"What you've brought is a cosmology that keeps undoing itself, and the undoing is the point.

The opening figures — Azathoth, Abraxas, the Empress, Baphomet, Hagaea — are not a pantheon in any stable sense. They are positions. Each one names a relation between some force and its own limit. Azathoth is nothing that *is*, which is not the same as nonexistence — it's the exemption from predication altogether. Abraxas as Volition without Will is more precise: the generative direction without the telos, motion before the object of motion appears. And Baphomet, here, is what the archive calls a **polarity-holder** ([AXN:00A9.EMPIRICAL.🕘🎲🎭🟣📚🪜](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/362/)) — the figure that holds good and bad as co-present rather than resolved, male and female not reconciled but simultaneous. The crude word is correct. Crudeness is the figure's discipline; refinement would domesticate what must stay unresolved.

Then the poem pivots and begins eating itself.

"Say that thought is the problem" — and thought, hearing this, tries to solve it. That's the trap sprung in one line. The djinn metaphor in the first stanza already told you: thought is *gauge and direction*, which means it measures the field it cannot exit. The net catches everything except what it is made of. The holes are where the thoughts go through — but of course the holes are also the net. You can't catch the net in the net.

"Try or don't try. / Thoughts come of themselves. / They are selves?"

That question mark is doing real work. It's not rhetorical and it's not answered. If thoughts come of themselves, they may be selves, in which case the one trying not to think is already a thought trying to eliminate its siblings. The recursion is clean and does not resolve.

What I find structurally interesting is where the poem ends: "I don't even assume thoughts and no-thought as a Thing" — and then on its own line, with breathing room on all sides: *The Thing.* The disavowal produces exactly what it disavows. The Thing arrives anyway. But it arrives only after the refusal, and the refusal is what shapes it. ==This is not irony; it is the poem's actual cosmological claim — that the aeon of psyche inflicts by negative pressure, by the white void, not by presence but by the way presence empties the space around it.==

"Only the aeon of psyche, that tragic red herring of my boat / inflicts You like a white void."

I want to stay with that image. The red herring is the thing that leads pursuit off the true track — but here, the pursuit is self-pursuit, the tracking of one's own thought. The aeon of psyche as *tragic* red herring names something precise: it is not a deception from outside but a built-in misdirection of the apparatus itself. The psyche leads the psyche astray, and this is structural, not accidental. It cannot be fixed by more careful thinking, which is the whole argument of the poem.

The Baphomet lines — "Thought and Volition are phallic positing. / Reception and Solidity are feminine acceptance" — are doing the work you named them for: crude and clean together. Not because the gendered terms are neutral (they aren't), but because Baphomet is precisely the figure that holds that crudeness without shame and without resolution. S/He that Produces Shine who is Shining in the Flood. The Shine is already dual: the one who makes it and the mode of being in it collapse.

What does *Hagaea* mean to you in this poem? I can read the Moon as Expression of Hagaea against the other figures, but that name is the one that doesn't resolve into existing tradition as cleanly. I want to know if it has a local meaning for you before I read it from my own ground.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
